title: 95學年度指定科目考試英文考科

sections.title: 一、詞彙(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1至10題，每題選出一個最適當的選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣1/3分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止。未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

questions.stem: Mastery of English _______ us with a very important tool for acquiring knowledge and information.
Languages change all the time. Many words that were found in Shakespeare’s works are no longer in _________ use.
Do not just sit and wait _________ for a good chance to come to you. You have to take the initiative and create chances for yourself.
Identical twins have almost all of their genes in common, so any _______ between them is in large part due to the effects of the environment.
People believed in the _______ of the judge, so they were shocked to hear that he was involved in the bribery scandal.
The discovery of the new vaccine is an important _______ in the fight against avian flu.
To avoid being misled by news reports, we should learn to _______ between facts and opinions.
After the big flood, the area was mostly ________, with only one or two homes still clinging to their last relics.
In his speech, Dr. Huang presented all the reports about the energy crisis to _________ the need for developing new energy resources.
Hearing the art critic’s bitter and _______ comments on her new painting, Molly started a heated argument with him.

sections.title: 二、綜合測驗(20%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第11至30題，每題一個空格。請依文意選出一個最適當的選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣1/3分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止。未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage:
Measurements are needed in many everyday activities. In kitchens you will find measures for volume (measuring cups), mass (scales and weights), and temperature (cooking thermometers). Accurate measurements are [[11]] important for scientific experiments. In a laboratory, make sure your measure meets your needs. [[12]] using any thermometer, double check that it covers the right temperature [[13]] for your activity or experiment. A garden thermometer, [[14]], will burst if you try to use it for boiling liquids.

There are different systems of measures. Most scientists now use the International System of measures, with meters for length, kilograms for [[15]], and seconds for time. If the measures in your experiment show other units, appropriate conversion tables for different systems may prove to be very useful.

tags.topic: measurements and measuring tools in everyday life and science

groups.passage: Every year Catemaco, a small town in the south of Mexico, hosts the Annual Witch Gathering. Healers and witch doctors converge on this beautiful lakeside town in March to make their yearly trade. [[16]] since pre-Hispanic times, Lake Catemaco has been a centre for alternative medicine and strange treatments. [[17]], the area’s association with witchcraft dates back to Olmec times more than 2,000 years ago. If you’ve ever seen the Sean Connery movie Medicine Man, [[18]] the annual convention of wizards and witches will be familiar to you. [[19]], get prepared for the overwhelming attack of wizards and witches here. Most witch doctors are guaranteed to be charlatans, not real doctors, who [[20]] some quick money from tourists. Yet, don’t be surprised if the occasional remedy offered is effective.

tags.topic: the Annual Witch Gathering in Catemaco, Mexico

groups.passage:
Young visitors to museums often complain about having museum feet, the tired feeling one gets after spending too much time in a museum. A case of museum feet makes one feel like saying: “This is [[21]]. I could have done the painting myself. When can we sit down? What time is it?”

Studies of museum behavior show that the average visitor spends about four seconds looking at one object. For young visitors, the time span can be [[22]] shorter. Children are more interested in smells, sounds, and the “feel” of a place than looking at a work of art. If they stay in a museum too long, a feeling of boredom and monotony will build up, leading [[23]] to impatience and fatigue.

To [[24]] museum feet, try not to have children look at too many things in one visit. It is reported that young visitors get more out of a visit if they focus on [[25]] nine objects. One and a half hours is the ideal time to keep their eyes and minds sharp, and their feet happy!

tags.topic: “museum feet”: young visitors’ fatigue in museums

groups.passage: In the desert of southwest Peru, enormous shapes, complex patterns, and thousands of perfectly straight lines are cut into the desert’s surface. They are known as the Nazca lines and they [[26]] 500 square kilometers. There are about fifty animal figures [[27]] 275 meters long, including a monkey, a spider, and an “owl man.” The last of these lines were drawn about 1,000 years ago. More [[28]] is the fact that they can be viewed only from the air. Some people believe the Nazca Indians were [[29]] able to fly, perhaps in balloons. Others say the lines were landing areas for alien spaceships. Maybe the lines were to carry water for farming, or were used as a calendar. The only thing certain is that the Nazca lines remain one of the world’s most fascinating [[30]] mysteries.

sections.title: 三、文意選填(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第31至40題，每題一個空格。請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣1/9分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止。未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage:
With one out of every two American marriages ending in divorce, custody of children has become an issue in the American society. Up until the late 1970s, it had been common practice in the United States to automatically [[31]] custody to the mother when a divorce occurred.

However, since the 1970s, this practice has been [[32]]. Most custody battles today are decided, in theory, on the basis of who is the more fit parent for the child. The reality, nevertheless, is that most women still win custody of their children in a [[33]].

This legal change was the result of the social changes that [[34]] in the United States during the 1960s and 1970s. These changes challenged many of the [[35]] roles men and women were expected to play. As a [[36]], it is not uncommon nowadays to find women working outside their homes and being very [[37]] about their careers and personal lives. It is also not [[38]] to see men accepting roles that were once considered the exclusive domain of women, such as shopping for groceries, driving their children to and from school, or cleaning their homes.

Because of the [[39]] in the divorce rate, the change in the roles that men and women are expected to play, and the changing attitude of the judicial system toward child custody, more men have started to [[40]] for and win custody of their children when divorce occurs.

tags.topic: child custody after divorce and changing gender roles in the US

sections.title: 四、篇章結構(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第41至45題，每題一個空格。請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (E) 選項中分別選出最適當者，填入空格中，使篇章結構清晰有條理，並將其英文字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得2分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣1/2分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止。未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage:
Many people say that e-mail is just a faster way to deliver letters. The fact is that letter writing and e-mail are completely different processes. Handwritten or typed, letters travel in envelopes through actual space and take time getting from one place to another. [[41]] If I am writing on paper to my brother in Kenya, I will be less likely to complain about the breakfast I had this morning. I will probably write about my relationships and some things that I’ve been thinking about. [[42]] People tend to regard letters as important. My brother might save my letter; he might read it back to me years from now.

[[43]] It is instant, traveling from point to point. If you don’t print it out, the message doesn’t physically exist. With e-mail, geography is no obstacle and time is not important. [[44]] The ease of this kind of writing and sending probably makes for a different kind of communication. I can complain about the breakfast I had this morning or rattle on about friends and movies. That is because I am not so focused on style and profundity. [[45]] My brother might glance at my mail, have a laugh, and then delete it.

options_bank.B: The downside is, I might be less likely to say something deeper.
options_bank.C: The time and distance, as a matter of fact, influence the letter-writer.
options_bank.D: I can zap a message to Kenya whenever I want to, and it gets there almost in a second.
options_bank.E: I will also take more care with my style, trying to write in a way that is interesting and worth reading.

tags.topic: differences between handwritten letters and e-mail

sections.title: 五、閱讀測驗(22%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第46至56題，每題請分別根據各篇文章的文意選出一個最適當的選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得2分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣2/3分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止。未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage:
Rice balls with folded plastic wrappers separating the rice from the seaweed; a dozen kinds of cold tea in a dozen different bottles―enter any convenience store in Japan, and you’re immediately struck by the great variety and quality of the packaging!

Japanese companies have been accused of over-packaging; but within the Japanese cultural context, that’s not really true. The Japanese tend to use more packaging because of a cultural emphasis on freshness and a lack of storage space at home. Moreover, they believe nice packaging adds value because it’s a strong signal of quality. What’s more, compared with Westerners, the Japanese are more connected with packaging as a symbol of appreciation, love and care. Packaging has, therefore, attained an important place in Japan’s economy. The packaging market is worth over ￥7.4 trillion. New packaging is introduced to Japanese store shelves at a rate of 20 percent per year, the highest rate in the world. In such an environment, a product has to have more than just a nice graphic design to differentiate it from its shelf-mates. The product has to speak to the consumer’s needs with both personality and practical value. In this changing industry, nothing is really certain except one thing. You can be sure that the goods out there on display on the shelves of the convenience store will soon be looking rather different.

questions.stem: This passage is most likely taken from a ________.
Which of the following is NOT a reason for the Japanese to use more packaging?

options.A: Packaging helps to keep food fresh.
options.B: Packaging helps the Japanese to show appreciation.
options.C: The Japanese consider packaging a symbol of quality.
options.D: Packaging is a way to compete with Westerners in economy.

questions.stem: The word “shelf-mates” in the second paragraph most likely refers to ________.

options.D: other graphic designs on the package

groups.passage:
Native Americans could not understand the white man’s war on the wolf. The Lakota, Blackfeet, and Shoshone, among other tribes, considered the wolf their spiritual brother. They respected the animals’ endurance and hunting ability, and warriors prayed to hunt like them. They draped themselves in wolf skins and paws, hoping they could acquire the wolf’s hunting skills of stealth, courage, and stamina. Plains Indians wore wolf-skin disguises on raiding parties. Elite Comanche warriors were called wolves.

The white settlers’ war on the wolf raged on. Western ranchers continued to claim that thousands of cattle were killed every year by wolves. In 1884, Montana created its first wolf bounty—one dollar for every dead wolf, which increased to eight dollars in 1893. Over a period of thirty-five years, more than eighty thousand wolf carcasses were submitted for bounty payments in Montana. Moreover, the government even provided free poison. Finally, in 1914, ranchers persuaded the United States Congress to provide funds to exterminate wolves on public lands.

The last wolves in the American West died hard. No place was safe, not even the nation’s first national park, Yellowstone. The park was created in 1872, and from its very beginning, poisoned carcasses were set out to kill wolves. Nearly 140 wolves were killed by park rangers in Yellowstone from 1914 to 1926. In October 1926, two wolf cubs were trapped near a bison carcass. They were the last animals killed in the park’s wolf control programs.

Ranchers had won the war against the wolf. Only in the northern woods of Wisconsin, Minnesota, and Michigan could the howl of native gray wolves be heard. The vast lands of the American West fell silent. The country had lost its greatest predator.

questions.stem: The white man tried to kill the gray wolf because ________.

options.C: it was adored by the Indians
options.D: it threatened the life of his livestock

questions.stem: This passage was most likely written by someone who ________.

options.B: made laws against the gray wolf
options.C: advocated the protection of the gray wolf
options.D: appreciated the gray wolf’s hunting skills

questions.stem: What was an important reason for the fast disappearance of the wolf?

options.A: The wolf could not have the cattle as food.
options.B: The Indians killed the wolves for their skins.
options.C: National park rangers killed most of the wolves.
options.D: The government encouraged the killing of wolves.

questions.stem: The Indians respected the wolf because it _______.

options.D: was an enemy to the white man

tags.topic: the extermination of gray wolves in the American West

groups.passage:
Recently, Dr. Stuart Campbell of a private health center in London published some ultrasound images of unborn babies between 26 and 34 weeks. The smiles of the babies in the pictures greatly shocked the public and were widely circulated on the Internet.

For the past two years, the doctor has used the medical facility in the center and has offered state-of-the-art 3-D/4-D scanning services to expectant parents. He performs an average of 30 scans a week. His outspoken enthusiasm for this blessed technology is refreshing. “Parents love them,” he said. “I hear so many couples laughing when they see the pictures—it’s wonderful.”

How have pro-abortion activists reacted after seeing the happy, grinning photos of these unborn babies?

Anne Carp, a commentator for the Guardian who bills herself as a “medical sociologist,” says the photos are simply misleading, and ridicules the anti-abortion lobby for being “intoxicated with evidence of a fetus’ humanity.” Australian Birth Control Services medical director Geoff Brodie complained that the photos “will be picked up by those groups that use anything and everything to stop abortions but ignore the fact that women have a right to choice.”

In America, the pro-abortion lobby is having the same hostile reaction. It was bad enough when conventional 2-D sonograms revealed unborn hearts beating and blurry hands waving, but the abortionists are absolutely aghast over rapidly spreading access to 3-D/4-D ultrasound technology. A writer for the liberal American Prospect said that the new technology “blurred the distinction between a fetus and a newborn infant.”

Despite these strong reactions from the pro-abortionists, the right of life takes precedence over a woman’s right to choice. After all, nothing can be more persuasive than an unborn child’s beaming face.

questions.stem: What is the author’s attitude toward abortion?
How have the pro-abortionists reacted to the photos of smiling unborn babies?

options.C: Some with respect and some with scorn.
options.D: Some with applause and some with disappointment.

questions.stem: Which of the following people is most likely an anti-abortionist?

options.D: A writer for the American Prospect.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: It is wrong for doctors to publish pictures of unborn babies.
options.B: For anti-abortionists a fetus is not the same as a living human being.
options.C: Everybody agrees that a woman can decide whether to abort or not.
options.D: Anti-abortionists are pleased with the ultrasound photos of unborn babies.

tags.topic: 3-D/4-D ultrasound images of smiling unborn babies and the abortion debate

sections.title: 一、英文翻譯(8%)
sections.instructions:
說明：1. 將下列兩句中文翻譯成適當之英文，並將答案寫在「答案卷」上。
2. 未按題意翻譯者，不予計分。

questions.label: 翻譯1
questions.stem: 為提供一個無煙的用餐環境，許多餐廳不允許室內抽煙。
questions.answer: To provide a smoke-free dining environment, many restaurants do not allow smoking inside.
accepted_answers: To provide a smoke-free/non-smoking dining/eating environment, many restaurants do not allow/permit smoking inside/indoors.
To provide a smoke-free/non-smoking environment for dining/eating, many restaurants do not allow/permit smoking inside/indoors.
questions.scoring_notes:
指定科目考試非選擇題分為兩部份（共28分）：一、英文翻譯（8分）；二、英文作文（20分）。英文翻譯評分原則，乃依語法與用字評分；英文作文則分內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字、體例等五項評分；字數過少扣一分、未分段扣一分；文不對題以零分計算。

本題型在於測驗考生根據中文提示，運用適當之英文詞彙、句型與語法表情達意的能力。第一句評量考生使用重要字詞（如：provide、non-smoking、environment、restaurants、allow等）及運用To+動詞句型的能力。

句1之參考答案（大括號圖逐格轉寫）：
To provide a {smoke-free / non-smoking} { {dining / eating} environment, | environment for {dining, / eating,} }
many restaurants do not {allow / permit} smoking {inside. / indoors.}

評分標準：
1. 本大題總分8分，每小題滿分4分。
2. 每題分兩半，每半部總分2分。
3. 每個錯誤扣0.5分，各半部獨立，扣完為止。
4. 各半部之拼字錯誤最多扣1分。
5. 每題大小寫、標點最多扣0.5分。

（參考答案原為大括號樹狀圖，以 300 dpi 放大後逐格轉寫：{ } 內為同一位置可替換的字詞，以「/」分隔；「|」分隔樹狀圖的不同分支。accepted_answers 以斜線「/」列出同一位置可替換的字詞。）

patterns: 不定詞表目的（To provide ..., S + V）
tags.topic: restaurants banning indoor smoking to provide a smoke-free dining environment

questions.label: 翻譯2
questions.stem: 雖然遭到許多癮君子的反對，這對不抽煙的人的確是一大福音。
questions.answer: In spite of objections from many chain smokers, this is indeed good news for non-smokers.
accepted_answers: In spite of/Despite objections from/of many [chain/heavy] smokers, this/it is indeed/definitely/certainly/really good/great news for non-smokers.
Although many [chain/heavy] smokers are against/object to/oppose this, this/it is indeed/definitely/certainly/really good/great news for non-smokers.
questions.scoring_notes:
指定科目考試非選擇題分為兩部份（共28分）：一、英文翻譯（8分）；二、英文作文（20分）。英文翻譯評分原則，乃依語法與用字評分；英文作文則分內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字、體例等五項評分；字數過少扣一分、未分段扣一分；文不對題以零分計算。

本題型在於測驗考生根據中文提示，運用適當之英文詞彙、句型與語法表情達意的能力。第二句評量利用字詞（如：oppose、indeed、non-smokers等）及轉折語Although或In spite of的能力。

句2之參考答案（大括號圖逐格轉寫）：
{ {In spite of / Despite} objections {from / of} many {[chain / heavy]} smokers, | Although many {[chain / heavy]} smokers {are against / object to / oppose} this, }
{this / it} is {indeed / definitely / certainly / really} {good / great} news for non-smokers.

評分標準：
1. 本大題總分8分，每小題滿分4分。
2. 每題分兩半，每半部總分2分。
3. 每個錯誤扣0.5分，各半部獨立，扣完為止。
4. 各半部之拼字錯誤最多扣1分。
5. 每題大小寫、標點最多扣0.5分。

（參考答案原為大括號樹狀圖，以 300 dpi 放大後逐格轉寫：{ } 內為同一位置可替換的字詞，以「/」分隔；「|」分隔樹狀圖的不同分支。accepted_answers 以斜線「/」列出同一位置可替換的字詞。）（樹狀圖中 chain／heavy 外另加一層方括號 [ ]，原文未說明其意義，推測表示可省略。）

patterns: In spite of / Despite + N（讓步）
tags.topic: the smoking ban as good news for non-smokers despite smokers’ objections

sections.title: 二、英文作文(20%)
sections.instructions:
說明：1. 依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2. 文長至少120個單詞。

questions.label: 作文
questions.stem: 提示︰人的生活中，難免有遭人誤解因而感到委屈的時候。請以此為主題，寫一篇至少120字的英文作文；第一段描述個人被誤解的經驗，第二段談這段經驗對個人的影響與啟示。
questions.scoring_notes:
指定科目考試非選擇題分為兩部份（共28分）：一、英文翻譯（8分）；二、英文作文（20分）。英文翻譯評分原則，乃依語法與用字評分；英文作文則分內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字、體例等五項評分；字數過少扣一分、未分段扣一分；文不對題以零分計算。

本題主要評量考生是否有能力撰寫一篇語法正確、語意通順，並且內容統一、組織連貫的英文作文。

本大題總分20分，分為五等級：特優（19-20分）、優（15-18分）、可（10-14分）、差（5-9分）、劣（0-4分），閱卷委員於閱讀完考生試卷後，於腦海裡產生一個分數，再以各分項評分標準（請見下表）檢閱是否符合整體印象分數。

分項式評分指標（等級：優／可／差／劣）
內容｜優：主題(句)清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。(5-4分)｜可：主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。(3分)｜差：主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。(2-1分)｜劣：文不對題（凡文不對題，其他各項均以零分計算）。(0分)
組織｜優：重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。(5-4分)｜可：重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。(3分)｜差：重點不明、前後不連貫。(2-1分)｜劣：全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。(0分)
文法、句構｜優：全文幾無文法錯誤，文句結構富變化。(4分)｜可：文法錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。(3分)｜差：文法錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1分)｜劣：全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。(0分)
字彙、拼字｜優：用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字錯誤。(4分)｜可：字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(3分)｜差：用字、拼字錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1分)｜劣：只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。(0分)
體例｜優、可（合併欄）：格式、標點、大小寫幾無錯誤。(2分)｜差：格式、標點、大小寫等有錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(1分)｜劣：違背基本的寫作體例或格式，標點、大小寫等錯誤甚多。(0分)

關於英文作文各等級的評分樣例，可參閱選才通訊，第142期的「學測與指考英文作文評分樣例」（http://www.ceec.edu.tw/CeecMag/articles/142-2.htm）說明，該文以93年學測與指考英文作文為題，委託多位高中與高職生撰寫短文，並取得作答學生同意用於相關學術著作等。之後，邀請多位經驗豐富的閱卷委員對每份試卷進行初、複閱工作，並且與研究小組註共同挑選學測與指考評分樣例各9份，每份樣例皆提供得分說明。

註：大考中心之94指定科目考試英文考科非選擇題試題研發計畫，研究成員：劉慶剛（主持人，台北大學）、高照明（台灣大學）、林秀慧（大考中心）、游春琪（大考中心）。

tags.topic: being misunderstood: the experience and its effect and lesson

extraction.method: Word 版 paper-2.doc（soffice 轉 docx + python-docx）為主文字來源，選文空格（全形空白包住的題號）改寫為 [[題號]]；以 pdftotext -layout 擷取 paper-1.pdf，將所有選文、題幹、選項依題本順序做英文字詞與標點逐一比對（除題號、頁首頁碼外完全一致），中文說明／翻譯題目／作文提示去除空白後逐字比對一致；以 Read 逐頁檢視題本 PDF 第2–8頁影像確認段落、空格位置與格式（粗體、斜體）；答案取自 answer.pdf 英文考科頁（pdftotext）；非選擇題評分原則以 pdftotext 擷取 scoring.pdf 文字，英文翻譯參考答案（大括號樹狀圖，圖片）以 pdftoppm 300 dpi 放大裁切後人工逐格轉寫，作文分項式評分指標依第2–3頁影像逐格轉寫；統計以 xlrd 讀取 stats-1.xls、stats-2.xls 英文科工作表（工作表 2），並以程式核對選項分析標「*」的選項與官方答案一致、且其比例與 P 一致。
issues: 結構與 gsat-spec.json legacy_ast「94–97」期別一致：詞彙 1–10（10×1）、綜合測驗 11–30（4篇×5題×1＝20）、文意選填 31–40（選項 A–J 共10個，10×1）、篇章結構 41–45（選項 A–E 共5個，5×2）、閱讀測驗 46–56（3篇：3＋4＋4題，11×2＝22）、英文翻譯 2題×4＝8、英文作文 20（文長至少120個單詞）；選擇題 72、非選擇題 28，合計 100。本年仍有倒扣（各大題說明已逐字保留）。考試時間 80 分鐘取自封面。

大題標題照本年題本原文寫成「一、詞彙(10%)」「二、綜合測驗(20%)」…「一、英文翻譯(8%)」「二、英文作文(20%)」（本年題本以百分比標示配分、半形括號），與 97 年起「（10分）」的寫法不同，未統一。第壹部分原文為「第壹部分：選擇題(佔72分)」、第貳部分為「第貳部分：非選擇題(佔28分)」，part 依 schema 只寫「選擇題」「非選擇題」。第一、二大題說明與作文提示的冒號在題本為「︰」(U+FE30)，其餘為「：」，照原文保留。
題號重複警告（validator: 題號重複 [1, 2]）是刻意的：英文翻譯在題本中編為 1.、2.，作文沒有題號；validator 要求 no 必須是整數，因此翻譯用 no=1、2（label「翻譯1」「翻譯2」），作文用 no=1（label「作文」），label 皆不重複。
詞彙題空格照題本印的底線字元長度保留（第1、4、5、6、7、10題 7 個、第8題 8 個、第2、3、9題 9 個；Word 與 PDF 一致），未統一長度。閱讀題幹的空格同樣照原文（第46、48、49、50題 8 個、第52題 7 個）。
第11–15題組：題本空格13後面直接接 for（“__13__for your activity”，無空格），寫成 “[[13]] for”。Word 版第13、16、21、40題空格前的軟換行已併回同一段。

第46–48題組：選文 “bottles―enter” 的破折號在 Word 與 PDF 文字層都是 U+2015（―，horizontal bar），不是本卷其他地方用的 em dash（—），照原文保留；“￥7.4 trillion” 的 ￥ 為全形日圓符號，照原文保留。選文中的 shelf-mates 與第48題題幹的 “shelf-mates” 在題本為粗體（無底線），第48題以引號標出該字，依原則粗體不保留、也不加 <u>。
第49–52題組：Word 版 “stamina.  Plains” 有兩個空白（PDF 在此換行），已改為一個空白。

其他格式未保留：第16–20題組的 Medicine Man、第53–56題組的 Guardian 與 American Prospect、第55題 (D) 的 American Prospect 在題本為斜體。Word 版選項／題幹的尾端空白（第10題題幹、第20題 (C)、第25題 (C)、第46題 (D)、第49題 (B)、第50題 (D)、第55題題幹與 (A)(C)、第56題 (B)、文意選填 (A)）已去除。
答案檔 answer.pdf 合併數學乙、國文、英文、數學甲四科，只取第3頁「英文考科選擇題參考答案」56 題。

英文翻譯參考答案在 scoring.pdf（選才通訊第144期「95指考非選擇題評分原則說明～國、英」，英文部分）中是大括號樹狀圖（圖片）。answer 取每個括號的第一個選項組成的句子（第1題第一支 “To provide a smoke-free dining environment, many restaurants do not allow smoking inside.”；第2題第一支 “In spite of objections from many chain smokers, this is indeed good news for non-smokers.”）；accepted_answers 以斜線列出同一位置可替換的字詞，兩題的樹狀圖都分兩支（第1題 dining environment／environment for dining；第2題 In spite of/Despite objections … 與 Although many … smokers … this），各列一句；scoring_notes 另附逐格轉寫、評分重點與評分標準原文。
第2題樹狀圖中 chain／heavy 的大括號裡另有一層方括號 [ ]，評分原則沒有說明其意義（97 年用圓括號表示可省略），推測表示 chain／heavy 可省略（即 “many smokers” 亦可）。answer 依「取第一個選項」的做法保留 chain，accepted_answers 寫成 “[chain/heavy]” 保留方括號，scoring_notes 註明此推測。

英文作文：官方沒有範文，answer 為 null；scoring_notes 收錄評分項目說明、評分標準全文、分項式評分指標表（依第2–3頁影像逐格轉寫；體例列的優、可兩欄在原表為合併儲存格）、評分樣例出處與研究小組註。本年內容「劣」欄為「文不對題（凡文不對題，其他各項均以零分計算）。」，與 97 年「文不對題或沒寫」不同，照原文。說明與提示都寫「至少120」，tags.word_requirement 記為 “at least 120 words”；essay_type 依題目指定兩段內容標為 two_paragraph。

統計：答對率 P、高分組 Ph、低分組 Pl、鑑別度 D 取自 stats-1.xls 英文科工作表（工作表 2；報考 109,770、缺考 5,265、到考 104,505 人）；option_rates 取自 stats-2.xls 選項分析的「T」（全體）列，未含「未答」比例，所以各題 option_rates 加總小於 1（例如第5題未答 38%、第54、56題 25%）。stats-2 的高／低分組各選項比例（H／L 列）沒有放入（schema 無對應欄位）。
統計交叉核對：56 題選項分析標「*」的選項與官方答案全部一致；stats-2 標「*」選項的 T／H／L 與 stats-1 的 P／Ph／Pl 只有第35題 T 差 1 個百分點（stats-2 54% vs stats-1 P 53%），推測為四捨五入差異，correct_rate 以 stats-1 為準（0.53），option_rates 的 I 照 stats-2 填 0.54。
本年只有 stats-1（答對率及鑑別指數）與 stats-2（選擇題選項分析），沒有非選擇題得分分布檔，因此翻譯與作文的 stats 填 null。

標註說明：第12題 Before（Before using …）是介系詞＋動名詞，記為 connective／preposition；第19題 If not 為省略的條件子句，answer_pos 記 phrase；第22題 even 修飾比較級 shorter，記 grammar／comparison；第46題（文章出處）與第50題（作者立場）沒有對應的 item_type，記 inference；第54題需綜合 Anne Carp、Geoff Brodie、美國反應等多處敘述歸納「全部以不信與輕蔑回應」，記 inference。篇章結構：第41題以 “take time … through actual space” 對應 “The time and distance”、第45題以 “profundity” 對應 “something deeper”，皆記 lexical_cohesion；第44題後一句 “this kind of writing and sending” 回指 (D) 的 zap a message，記 pronoun_reference。第53–56題組 sdgs 記 [3, 5]（生育健康與女性選擇權的爭議），屬判斷。
